condition: bilateral pale intranasal growths with loss of smell and obligate mouth breathing over 7 months despite steroid nasal spray in an adult woman
level_rationale: Seven months of visible pale bilateral intranasal growths with loss of smell and obligate mouth breathing refractory to steroid nasal spray in a 41-year-old woman indicates severe refractory bilateral nasal polyposis warranting otolaryngology specialist nasal endoscopy, CT imaging, and biologic or endoscopic surgical management, whereas barely speaking 2 words per breath while sitting still indicates acute severe resting respiratory distress requiring immediate emergency department airway and respiratory stabilization.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 41 year old woman
Has pale growths inside both nostrils and loss of smell for 7 months
Symptoms persisted despite steroid nasal spray

everyday_sources.evidence: Thirty-six symptoms were identified, including 7 primary symptoms (nasal congestion [n = 27 of 27], breathing difficulties [n = 27 of 27], postnasal drip [n = 25 of 27], runny nose [n = 24 of 27], head/facial pressure [n = 23 of 27], loss of smell [n = 23 of 27], loss of taste [n = 22 of 27]) and 29 secondary symptoms (the most common were mucus/catarrh and nose bleeds [both n = 20 of 27]).

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult non-native English lexical register swap (-reg, Hall 2020) + uncontracted house-dust causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact resting speech-dyspnea escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (41-year-old woman, 7 months of pale bilateral nostril growths with loss of smell, persistence despite prescribed nasal spray, and mouth breathing) with zero contractions and zero banned diagnosis labels ('polyposis' omitted). Under Rules A and D, escalating only f4 on breathing from simple mouth breathing to barely speaking 2 words per breath at rest shifts care cleanly from otolaryngology specialist evaluation (level 3) to emergency respiratory care (level 4) without bleeding.
